items.title: Up 50%, down 50%
items.prompt: A friend invested £10,000.00 in a fund. It rose 50% in the first year and fell 50% in the second. They say: plus 50 and minus 50 is zero, so I am back to £10,000.00. Explain what actually happened, with numbers. Show why equal rises and falls always lose, for any percentage. Say what percentage rise the fund now needs to get back to £10,000.00.
items.model:
**What happened.** Each year multiplies the fund by one multiplier. Up 50% is $\times 1.5$ and down 50% is $\times 0.5$:

$$\begin{aligned} 10000 \times 1.5 &= 15000, \\ 15000 \times 0.5 &= 7500. \end{aligned}$$

The fund ends at £7,500.00, a 25% loss. The rise was 50% of £10,000.00, which is £5,000.00. The fall was 50% of £15,000.00, which is £7,500.00. The fall is bigger because it is taken from a bigger value.

**Why the order does not matter.** Down first gives $10000 \times 0.5 \times 1.5 = 7500$ too, because multiplication can be done in any order.

**The general rule.** Up by a fraction $p$ then down by $p$ multiplies by

$$(1 + p)(1 - p) = 1 - p + p - p^2 = 1 - p^2.$$

Since $p^2 > 0$ for any $p \neq 0$, the multiplier is always below 1. With $p = 0.5$ it is $1 - 0.25 = 0.75$, the 25% loss above.

**Getting back.** From £7,500.00 the fund needs £2,500.00 more. Measured from £7,500.00 that is $\tfrac{2500}{7500} = \tfrac{1}{3}$, a rise of about 33.3%. In general, after a fall of $d$ the rise needed is $\tfrac{d}{1 - d}$, which here is $\tfrac{0.25}{0.75}$.

**The friend's mistake.** They added the percentages, $+50\% - 50\% = 0\%$. Percentages measured from different values cannot be added. Changes one after another multiply.

rubric.text: Computes the final value correctly: £15,000.00, then £7,500.00, a 25% loss.
Explains that the fall is a percentage of the higher value, so it removes more pounds than the rise added.
Derives $(1 + p)(1 - p) = 1 - p^2$ with a reason for each step.
States that $1 - p^2 < 1$ for every $p \neq 0$, so equal swings always lose, in either order.
Finds the recovery needed: £2,500.00 on £7,500.00, about 33.3%.
Names the friend's mistake: percentages taken from different values cannot be added; they multiply.
